sections.title: PART A · Section A: Reading. Answer in ONE word.

questions.q: What kind of water can we drink?
What becomes the only hope when wells dry up?
Where should rainwater from rooftops be sent back?

sections.passage:
Water covers most of our planet, yet only a tiny part of it is fresh water that we can drink. Rivers, lakes and underground water are shared by people, animals and plants. In many Indian towns, women and children still walk long distances every morning to fetch a few pots of water. During summer the wells dry up and tankers become the only hope.
Much of this shortage is caused by our own carelessness. Taps are left running, pipes leak for weeks and rainwater simply flows away into drains. Factories pour waste into rivers and make the water unfit for use. Farmers often grow crops that need a great deal of water even in dry regions.
The good news is that simple steps can make a big difference. Rainwater harvesting allows us to collect the rain from rooftops and send it back into the ground. Repairing leaks, closing taps while brushing and reusing the water used for washing vegetables to water plants can save hundreds of litres every week. If every family saves a little, the whole community will have enough.

questions.q: Find words from the passage that mean: (a) not enough (b) surprised

sections.passage:
Every year thousands of migratory birds travel to India from cold countries such as Siberia and Central Asia. When winter covers their homes with ice and snow, food becomes scarce, so they fly thousands of kilometres to warmer lands. Wetlands like Bharatpur in Rajasthan and Chilika Lake in Odisha become lively with flamingos, cranes, ducks and pelicans.
Scientists are still amazed at how these birds find their way. They seem to use the position of the sun and stars, the earth's magnetic field and familiar landmarks such as rivers and mountains. Many of them fly in a V-shape, which saves energy because each bird is helped by the air moving off the wings of the bird ahead.
Sadly, these visitors face many dangers. Wetlands are being drained for buildings and farms, lakes are polluted, and some birds are hunted illegally. Power lines and tall towers also cause deaths. Protecting wetlands and creating awareness among local people can ensure that our winged guests keep returning every year.

sections.title: Section B: Writing. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: You are Aman of Class X. Write an article (150–200 words) for your school magazine on 'The Importance of Reading Books'. Use these clues: knowledge and imagination — vocabulary and language — good habits and values — books as friends — reducing screen time — libraries.
questions.answer: Points for a good answer: title and by-line; introduction (books open the world to us); body — books increase knowledge and imagination, improve vocabulary and language, teach values through stories and lives of great people, are faithful friends that relax and comfort us, and offer a healthy break from mobile screens; suggest reading daily, visiting libraries and sharing books; conclusion (make reading a lifelong habit). Write in 3–4 paragraphs within 150–200 words.

or.q: You are Kavya of Class X. Write a report (150–200 words) for your school magazine on the Tree Plantation Drive organised by your school's Eco Club.
or.answer: Points: heading, by-line, date and place; who organised it and when; chief guest; number and kinds of saplings planted; participation of students, teachers and parents; slogans and awareness talk on the importance of trees; promise to look after the plants; conclusion on the success of the drive. Use the past tense and passive voice where suitable.

sections.title: Answer in about 100 words.

questions.q: You are Priya of 24, Lake Road, Bhopal. Write a letter (about 100 words) to the Editor of a national daily about the poor condition of roads in your area.
questions.answer: Format: sender's address, date, The Editor, newspaper name and address, subject (Poor condition of roads in Lake Road area), salutation 'Sir/Madam'. Body: potholes and broken roads; accidents and traffic jams; problems in the rainy season; request to the authorities through the newspaper to repair the roads quickly. Closing 'Yours faithfully, Priya'.

or.q: You are Sameer. Write an email (about 100 words) to your friend inviting him to your sister's wedding.
or.answer: Include: To, Subject (Invitation to my sister's wedding); greeting; date, time and venue; how much you want him to come; any arrangements (stay, travel); closing with your name. Keep it friendly and informal.

sections.title: Section D: Literature. Answer in about 40 words.

questions.q: How did the old man treat the boy for snake bite? (Snake Bite)
questions.answer: He made Raja sit still on Grandfather's lap, took water in a small brass vessel and recited mantras. After a few minutes he washed Raja's finger, gave him water to drink and asked him to keep quiet. Then he declared that Raja was out of danger.

or.q: What was the 'magic cure' that the grey-haired old man performed on Raja? Was it really a cure?
or.answer: He recited mantras over water in a brass vessel, then washed Raja's finger and gave him water to drink. It was not a real cure — Raja had only been stung by a bee and the pain had already stopped; the 'cure' was superstition.
